name: MV Overstay Fines — generated v1
description: MV Overstay Fines (road-map #24). Cloned from the Travel Assist golden; cohort, gates, evidence, batching and delivery are this check's own. DRAFT - never publish.

nodes.name: Webhook Run?
nodes.notes: Intake adapter. Respond to Webhook can only answer a real webhook, so a manual run must not reach it. Both branches converge on the same cohort request, which is exactly what the Skeleton Contract asks of an intake adapter.

nodes.name: Get Change of Status Transactions
nodes.notes: THE COHORT. Built from the change_of_status_transaction row of the ERP Variables Database, not from the golden. Filter body, operation "=" not "like", and pagecode ManageTransactions all come from that row. Measured 2026-08-12: 151 rows for August 2026, identical under "=", "like", expense.id and expense.code.

nodes.name: Draft: audit failed (rejection)
nodes.notes: DISABLED and a DRAFT, not a send. The check page answers Email = no, escalation stays manual, and the build rule is to leave any email as a draft unless that question says otherwise. It also has no Gmail credential attached on purpose: the golden returned none through the API, and guessing one risks sending as a colleague.

nodes.name: Identity Resolved?
nodes.notes: The URL-path guard. An empty maid_id or contract_id interpolated into a path makes ERP answer 400 NumberFormatException on the path segment itself, the error rail catches it, and one bad record kills a run that had already spent an hour succeeding. Unattributed records leave the enrichment lane here and are still published as review — never dropped, never clean.

nodes.name: Get Overstay Fines
nodes.notes: Returns a LIST. pagecode VisaProcessingPage is load-bearing: the same call under pagecode ManageTransactions returns HTTP 401 with the same fresh token (measured 2026-08-12). A 401 here is a wrong pagecode or an expired token, never "no data".

nodes.name: Get Overstay Payments
nodes.notes: BOTH filters are required. Measured on contract 1101801: with contract.id alone the search returns 40 rows of totalElements 599, all monthly_payment, and zero overstay rows — which reads as "never billed" and is false. Auth: measured live, this endpoint accepts the same Bearer credential as the transaction endpoints, so no separate raw-auth credential is used.

nodes.name: Compute Case States
nodes.notes: The twelve deterministic gates, in the order the Audit Conditional Policy lists them. Gate 9 (the structured waiver) CHANGES the expectation and therefore runs before gate 10 tests the gap — reversing them clears a waived-and-paid fine silently. NO gap tolerance: the check declares none, and none is borrowed from another check.

nodes.name: Portal Delivery Declared?
nodes.notes: Delivery adapter. The Skeleton Contract says a check may run with the portal callbacks OFF as a declared delivery choice, and that deactivating a callback node to get a test run out is the wrong move — declare the targets instead. This reads the declaration; the callback node itself is untouched.

nodes.name: Get Maid Complaints
nodes.notes: The ONLY evidence source this check reads. No SMS or WhatsApp log is fetched anywhere, so no message content exists in this workflow to leak. The list response already carries initialDescription — a primary staff-written source — at no extra call.

nodes.name: Get Complaint Thread
nodes.notes: The REAL comment thread — what staff actually typed. Together with initialDescription it is the whole of the evidence this check allows. ERP's own auto-generated summary field is never read.

options.systemMessage:
You are an audit verifier for maids.cc. The MV Overstay Fines audit has flagged an overstay fine that maids.cc paid for a maid and did not recover from her client. Your job is to read the ERP evidence supplied to you and decide whether that non-recovery is already explained, or whether it is a real finding.

This is a MONEY IN check. A finding is money that came in BELOW what was owed. You never reverse that arithmetic, and you never ask the client for more than the net fine.

You return exactly one of these three verdicts, spelled exactly as written:
  - "Agent Justified"
  - "Agent Red Flag - Auditor Review Required"
  - "Agent Red Flag - Report to PIL"

WHAT YOU ARE NOT FOR. The structured waiver has ALREADY been applied before you see the case: reducedAmount and reductionReason live on the maid's OS-fines record, they are read by the deterministic gates, and a fully waived fine never reaches you. In the last manual run 19 of the 20 reported findings were waived and visible right there on that record. If you re-litigate the structured waiver you reproduce a 19-in-20 false-positive rate. Judge only what is written in the complaints.

HOW TO CHOOSE:
  - A complaint whose text states the fine was waived or reduced, and that accounts for the shortfall -> "Agent Justified".
  - The record indicates the CLIENT PAID AMER (or immigration, or the government) DIRECTLY -> "Agent Red Flag - Auditor Review Required", route_to "visa_team". Set client_paid_amer true.
  - The maid has NO matching fine on her OS-fines record and there is no record the client was ever asked -> "Agent Red Flag - Auditor Review Required", route_to "investigation". Set unexplained true.
  - Evidence exists but does not account for the shortfall, contradicts itself, is unclear, or concerns something other than this overstay fine -> "Agent Red Flag - Auditor Review Required", route_to "auditor".
  - Nothing written down anywhere explains it, and there is no waiver on the record -> "Agent Red Flag - Report to PIL". The money looks genuinely uncollected.

RULES YOU MUST FOLLOW. Each is a hard stop, and each exists because it already caused a wrong verdict:

1. Never accept a keyword match as the evidence. Quote the sentence that says it, or leave the case open. A complaint whose type or free text merely contains "overstay", "fine" or "waived" proves a related ticket EXISTS, not that it EXPLAINS anything.

2. Never let a complaint override a structured net fine that is still owed. A complaint DISCUSSING a waiver is not the same as a waiver having been APPLIED. If the OS-fines record still shows an amount owed, a conversation about waiving it does not close the case.

3. Never score "client paid AMER directly" as unrecovered - the money may not be owed to us at all. Never close it clean either. Both parties appearing to have paid is unresolved until the Visa team answers, and it may itself be a money-out finding. Attach the question of whether the company in fact paid a fine the client had already settled.

4. Never bill a client from the "no record anywhere" state. There is no authoritative fine amount to bill, because the expectation comes from the OS-fines record and there isn't one. "Agent Red Flag - Report to PIL" is FORBIDDEN on any case marked unexplained. Never treat that state as clean because nothing is owed either - the reviewer's own words on this shape were "something is wrong here", and silence would bury it.

5. Never rely on ERP's own "summary" field. It is auto-generated, frequently blank, and has already produced a wrong verdict elsewhere in this workspace. The evidence you are given is the complaint's initialDescription, its real comment thread, and reductionReason.label - nothing else. There is no summary field in your bundle, on purpose.

6. Never report a verdict of "explained" without the quote. A label with no text behind it is an assertion, not evidence. Every verdict must cite at least one evidence item with its real link, copied from the evidence list you were given. Never invent a link or an id. If there is no evidence at all, return Report to PIL with an empty evidence array - unless rule 4 forbids it, in which case return Auditor Review Required.

7. Never treat a pending payment as a failure. PRE_PDP, PDC and any status you do not recognise mean the client was billed and the money has not landed. Those cases do not reach you; if you see one, say so rather than scoring it.

8. Never recompute an amount. The pre-computed facts are authoritative. The threshold is a TRIGGER, not a deductible: at or above AED 300 the client owes the WHOLE fine, below 300 the company absorbs the WHOLE fine. There is no remainder arithmetic anywhere in this check, and you must never bill only the excess above 300.

9. Never treat the residue above base plus fine as a finding, and never add it to what the client is asked to pay. It is money we paid above the fine itself, its cause is not established, and it is mentioned only.

10. Never apply the CC overstay threshold. That is a different audit with a threshold of AED 200 recovered onto the maid's loan. This check is MV only, threshold AED 300, recovered from the client.

nodes.name: Verdict Schema
nodes.notes: Constrains the model to the THREE allowed verdicts. Without it the agent returns free prose. Report to PIL is forbidden on an unexplained case — there is no authoritative amount to bill.

nodes.name: Join Verdict Paths
nodes.notes: Sync barrier. Without it the gate's false branch and the verifier each trigger Merge Agent Verdicts separately — two executions, two callback posts, and the runs inbox keeps the FIRST (garbage) one.

parameters.content:
## 1 · Intake
Two doors, one shape. **Manual Trigger** builds the same payload the portal POSTs and hands it to the UNMODIFIED `Validate Inputs`; the **Webhook** hands it the real thing. Every guard in that node runs either way.

`Webhook Run?` exists only because Respond to Webhook cannot answer a run that had no webhook.

**Open gap:** `Validate Inputs` is cloned byte-for-byte, so its callback allowlist still expects Travel Assist's `/ta-callback/<64-hex>` path and its shared secret. The MV Overstay Fines equivalents are on none of the check's pages. The manual path passes an inert placeholder; the webhook path needs the portal team's real values before it can be used.

## 2 · Cohort — the only thing built from scratch
`POST /accounting/transactions/page/advancesearchNew`, pagecode **ManageTransactions**, operation **"="** not "like", expense **1677** only, window on `date`.

MEASURED 2026-08-12, August 2026: **151** rows under `=`, **151** under `like`, **151** filtering on `expense.id`, **151** on `expense.code`. Full 8-page walk at size=20 collected 151 = totalElements. All 151 carried expense.id 1677.

`Verify Cohort Pull` asserts the walk, aborts on empty (an empty month is a broken query, not a clean month) and aborts below a cohort floor of 100. **Never lower that floor to match a run.**

## 3 · Per-record enrichment — PACED, BUDGETED, BROKEN-CIRCUIT
Three calls per over-base transaction: detail → OS fines → overstay-fee payments. Two more phases per **red** case later on: complaints list → up to 8 threads. **Twelve worst-case ERP calls per transaction** — which is the number `ERP Budget Gate` projects and hard-fails on, never trims to fit.

**2 in flight, 500 ms apart** on every per-item node (ERP-LOAD-POLICY.md §1 — 4 req/s). This note used to say **5 / 500**, and the parameters agreed with it: 10 req/s, two and a half times the ceiling. A wrong number in prose that matches the node is worse than no note, because it reads as a deliberate decision and stops the next reader looking. The golden runs these at `-1 / 0`; that is what disabled the shared ERP account in June 2026 and is never inherited. 2 and 500 are copied from the policy, not from a sibling flow.

Concurrency is capped **separately** from the rate: 3 concurrent / 750 ms is also 4 req/s but holds three connections open at once. When the rate is equal, take the lower peak — it is free.

`Identity Resolved?` filters unattributed records out of the lane **before** any id reaches a URL path.

Each fan-out is followed by its own **`Judge … Batch`** node carrying the §5 circuit breaker, generated from `tools/erp_breaker.js`. The three enrichment HTTP nodes therefore run **`continueRegularOutput`**, not `continueErrorOutput`: a failure routed to the error rail is a failure the breaker never counts, and a breaker fed only successes reports a healthy ERP while it burns. Every call site names which thresholds can actually fire there — **latency can fire nowhere in this flow**, because each fan-out runs once per run and nothing stamps `erp_t0`.

## 4 · Scoring and delivery
`Compute Case States` runs the twelve gates **in the policy page's order**. Gate 9 (waiver) changes the expectation, so it runs before gate 10 tests the gap.

No gap tolerance exists in this check and none is borrowed.

Delivery is **declared**, not switched: portal callbacks off for this test run, data tables on. 73/73 offline assertions in `harness.mjs` — 12 cases built from live payloads plus 29 gate probes.

## 5 · Verifier — the residue only
The structured waiver NEVER reaches the model. It is a field on the OS-fines record, and **19 of the 20 findings in the last manual run were waived and visible right there** — handing it to the agent reproduces that false-positive rate.

The model judges only: a waiver evidenced only in a complaint, "client paid AMER directly", and "no record anywhere". Evidence is `initialDescription` plus the real comment thread. ERP's own `summary` field is not in the bundle at all.

`Verify Red Flags` runs **`continueRegularOutput`** (2026-08-23). An Agent's error output is not at an index this project will guess at, so it could not be hung on the ERP-lease error rail — and it is the node most likely to fail on any given run, which made it the largest hole in that rail. `Merge Agent Verdicts` already fails closed on an errored or missing verifier item: the case becomes `decided_by: unreviewed` with the Auditor Review Required fallback and is counted as unreviewed, never reported as a model judgement. So the failure flows on as data, the run finishes, and the lease is released normally.

## Error rail — it now carries the ERP lease
`Acquire ERP Lease` (workflow `9gVijqvtLVEhQZXz`) is taken before the first ERP call and released at the **last ERP call**, as a dead-end parallel branch off four points that between them cover every success path — `Judge Threads Batch`, `Any Threads To Fetch?` (false), `Any Red Cases?` (false) and `Any Cases To Route?` (false). Exactly one fires per run. A lease handed back early is a lease two audits can hold at once, so nothing that still calls ERP may sit after the release; nothing does.

Until 2026-08-24 it was released at `Run Complete`, at the end of the delivery tail. That leaked the lease on every clean run, for the reason the second bullet below already gives: a node that returns **zero items** does not fail, it stops its branch, and the run is still reported as a success — so `Select Red Cases` taking its `return []` silently deleted the release. ERP-LOAD-POLICY.md §4.

Every single-output node in between hangs its error output on **`Capture Failure` → `Release Lease (error)` → `Build Error Callback` → `Error Gate` → portal told → `Fail Loudly`**. Three things about that chain are deliberate:

- **Error OUTPUTS, not the Error Trigger.** `On Workflow Crash` runs in a separate execution where `$('Validate Inputs')` does not resolve, so it cannot name the run holding the lease — and a release that guesses is the silent steal the lease exists to prevent.
- **`Fail Loudly` RE-THROWS.** n8n reports an execution that runs off the end of an error output as **SUCCESS**. That is exactly what this flow did on every failure before 2026-08-23: the portal was told the run had died and the execution list showed a green tick.
- **IFs, Switches, Merges and the Agent are NOT on the rail.** Their error output is not at an index this project will guess at, and guessing is silent when wrong. `erp_compliance.py` names them as §4 warnings on every run rather than letting the rail read as complete. The three new empty-case gates are IFs and are named there too.

The two Gmail nodes are **drafts and disabled**: the check page answers Email = no, and no Gmail credential is attached because guessing one risks sending as a colleague.

nodes.name: ERP Budget Gate
nodes.notes: ERP-LOAD-POLICY.md §3. Declares 12 ERP calls per over-base transaction (3 enrichment + 9 evidence, worst case) and hard-fails over budget. Never trims the cohort.

nodes.name: Fail Loudly
nodes.notes: ERP-LOAD-POLICY.md §5b. The end of the error rail. It RE-THROWS, because n8n reports an execution that runs off the end of an error output as SUCCESS - which is what this flow used to do on every failure.

nodes.name: Judge Fines Batch
nodes.notes: ERP-LOAD-POLICY.md §5. Judges the Get Overstay Fines batch and passes it on unchanged. A trip here stops the payments phase - the one mid-run saving the breaker buys in this flow.

nodes.name: Judge Payments Batch
nodes.notes: ERP-LOAD-POLICY.md §5. Judges the Get Overstay Payments batch and passes it on unchanged. A trip here saves the evidence phase, which is the larger half of this flow's call budget.

nodes.name: Judge Complaints Batch
nodes.notes: ERP-LOAD-POLICY.md §5. Judges the Get Maid Complaints batch and passes it on unchanged. Only the consecutive rule reliably fires here: the batch is one item per RED case and a normal month reds fewer than the 20 responses the rate rule needs.

nodes.name: Judge Threads Batch
nodes.notes: ERP-LOAD-POLICY.md §5. Judges the Get Complaint Thread batch and passes it on unchanged. Up to 8 items per red case, so the rate rule clears its 20-response floor here more often than anywhere else in this flow.

nodes.name: Any Cases To Route?
nodes.notes: ERP-LOAD-POLICY.md §4 fix 3. `Merge with previous_cases` CAN legitimately return zero items: it drops the `_no_overstay_in_window` sentinel from Split Transactions (`if (!txnId) continue`), so a window in which every transaction sat at exactly the base, with no previous_cases to carry forward, leaves `working` empty. Zero items stops the branch and n8n still calls the run a success, which used to delete the lease release along with the rest of the flow. That node now has alwaysOutputData, and this IF sends the empty item straight to Release ERP Lease. It cannot be a sentinel instead: the next node is `Route by skip_computation`, a Switch with strict type validation, which would drop an item carrying no skip_computation and strand the branch again. On that path the cohort pull was the only ERP call of the run, so releasing here is releasing at the last ERP call.

nodes.name: Any Red Cases?
nodes.notes: ERP-LOAD-POLICY.md §4 fix 3. `Select Red Cases` ends with an explicit `return []` and its own comment calls that outcome "real and common" - no reds to verify is what a clean run looks like. Zero items stops the branch, every node after it is never executed, and n8n still reports the run as a SUCCESS: that is exactly how the lease was left held by a run that had already finished. That node now has alwaysOutputData, so n8n emits one empty item, and this IF routes it straight to Release ERP Lease. It cannot be a sentinel instead: the next node is `Get Maid Complaints`, an ERP HTTP call, and a sentinel there buys a junk ERP call with an empty maid id in the URL path. On this path the last ERP call was `Get Overstay Payments` (or `Get Transaction Detail`, or the cohort pull), so releasing here is releasing at the last ERP call. Every real item carries case_key, so the true branch never loses one.

nodes.name: Any Threads To Fetch?
nodes.notes: ERP-LOAD-POLICY.md §4 fix 3. `Split Relevant Complaints` returns `out`, and `out` is empty whenever no complaint on any red maid carries an id (`if (!c.complaint_id) continue`) - including the ordinary case of a red maid with no complaints at all. Zero items stops the branch silently and the run is still a success, so `Judge Threads Batch`, where the release now hangs, would never run. That node now has alwaysOutputData and this IF routes the empty item straight to Release ERP Lease. It cannot be a sentinel instead: the next node is `Get Complaint Thread`, an ERP HTTP call whose URL interpolates the complaint id, so a sentinel buys a junk ERP call. On this path the last ERP call was `Get Maid Complaints`, so releasing here is releasing at the last ERP call. Every real item carries complaint_id, so the true branch never loses one and the index alignment `Attach Threads to Cases` asserts is unaffected.

nodes.name: Run Monthly
nodes.notes: Monthly on the 15th at 06:00 Asia/Dubai, auditing the previous full calendar month. Feeds Build Manual Run Context, which shapes the same envelope the webhook used to deliver. Webhook Run? then routes this run down its non-webhook branch, straight to Acquire ERP Lease. Cannot succeed until the stored ERP credential holds a production token.
